findings.where: the `asked_a_motor_for` block of every region report, and the `not` field of the two sound logs
findings.what: The row asks that each of the thirty-odd feelings be identifiable by its haptic pattern alone with the screen face down, and nothing in the set shows a pattern reaching either a finger or an ear: all 14 motor asks across the three feeling scenes (7 in 07, 4 in 08, 3 in 15) answer 'no motor in a browser: the page rhythm carries it instead', the substitute that does carry it is the page visibly lifting and turning — which a face-down screen cannot deliver — and the other half of the substitute, the feeling's own sound, is in the clips only because the harness mixed the .ogg over silence, which 07_feeling_landing.sound.json states itself: "not": "a recording of the running app's audio output".
findings.why: With the screen face down the page-movement channel is gone by construction and the sound channel is never recorded coming from the app, so the row's central sensory claim — identifiable by pattern alone, face down — rests entirely on a model in logs/haptics.check.json and on asset files the app is never observed playing.

findings.artifact: logs/reception_picked_up.report.json (and the same field in all 16 other region reports)
findings.what: The pocket — one of the three ambient presence surfaces the reports name — reads back empty in every single report in the set, 17 of 17, including reception_picked_up.report.json, the record made expressly to pick the phone up after the pushes and read the pocket back; its accompanying text, "the browser is holding nothing" plus "a held list that is empty after the app has been opened is the surface working", cannot distinguish a pocket that was cleared from a pocket that was never filled.
findings.why: Three ambient presence surfaces are required and one of the three has no positive evidence anywhere in the set, only an explanation of why its measurement is empty.

findings.where: the notification toast at the bottom right of all three crops; `browser`, `records[0].silent` and the closing `note` in the log
findings.what: The only evidence of a state change being perceptible without opening the app is a Chromium desktop toast on a Linux virtual display reading '127.0.0.1:8796 • now / noor / said how they are' next to a blank grey placeholder icon — a text banner, i.e. a message in a different colour; the log records 20 worker-shown notifications with app_open false but the one stored record carries silent: true, and the log's own note says "this is not an iPhone banner, there is no lock screen in evidence, and what an installed iOS web app does with the same call is not shown anywhere in this build".
findings.why: The row asks for a non-haptic iOS substitute that reads as equally physical rather than as a missing feature; the closed-app surface in evidence is a silent line of generic text on a desktop browser, which reads as the absence of the sensation rather than as a substitute for it.

findings.where: frames 672-695 (the last take, the link coming back), the row above 'on my way - leaving in ten'; report row 8078, id 01M1MCJ1M079RT7T54CSV5QMJE, type message, tall 71, listed in `whole_on_the_glass`
findings.what: Of the two notes the far phone wrote while the link was cut, the state lands correctly ('— noor is quiet' appears at frame 672 and the standing line reads OUT HEADS DOWN QUIET) but the message lands as a completely empty sheet carrying only the signature 'teo' — the wrong name, since the far phone is noor — and the text 'the bus is late, dont wait up' appears nowhere in the remaining 24 frames; the same row is blank and identical in frames 673, 676, 682 and 695.
findings.why: This clip is the one artifact in the set that shows the far phone's state and words reaching this screen, and half of the thing it was built to show arrives with no content and the wrong author on it.

findings.where: frames 101-124, the hold on the 'pigeon' tile (24 frames at 80 ms = 1.92 s of app time)
findings.what: The gesture that sets a feeling's intensity produces almost nothing on the glass: after the family-tab switch settles at 400 ms, every frame to the end of the hold changes the whole picture by 0.027 to 0.037 grey levels of luma, and the cumulative change across 1.44 s is 0.17 grey levels; the growth that is there is confined to a 198 x 205 device-pixel tile (66 x 68 CSS px), where the ink area goes from 3,428 to 6,141 dark pixels.
findings.why: A feeling that is authored and charged by holding is only as legible as the charge is, and the sender cannot see how hard they are pressing; the scene's own note concedes it — "The picture the hold makes is still too small; the answer to that is in the app, not in the shutter speed."

findings.where: frames 21-76 of 08 against frames 0-55 of 07, phase correlation over the same top 700 device pixels (the standing-line sheet)
findings.what: The same feeling at the same strength moves the page by different amounts in the two clips: 'hold' lifts the page 16.14 px peak in 07 (asked amplitude 142/255) and 6.55 px peak in 08 (asked amplitude 143/255), a factor of 2.5; within 08 alone, 'hold' at 143/255 lifts 6.55 px while 'here' at 125/255 lifts 14.24 px — the lower ask moves the page more than twice as far. The control is clean: 'here' at 0.80 measures 14.23 px in 07 and 14.24 px in 08.
findings.why: If the size of the sensation does not track the strength the sender chose, intensity is not part of what is transmitted, and nothing in the reports carries a field that would explain the difference.

findings.where: the 100 x 100 CSS-px bottom-right corner of each still, just above the tab strip; and 15's frames 0-15 and 200-215
findings.what: The dog-ear corner that opens the feeling picker is on the glass in 9 of the 10 stills and absent from 14_media_viewer; it is shown actually opening in only 2 of the 5 regions (US and Pulse); and 'one gesture' cannot be checked at all — no pointer is drawn in any frame, and reaching a feeling outside the default family runs openCorner, then a family tab, then a hold, then a release as four separate acts.
findings.why: The row asks for a feeling in one gesture from any region; the affordance is there almost everywhere but the gesture count and the coverage of the remaining three regions are not in the evidence.

findings.where: the picker frames 102-124 and the two arrivals at frames 216-321 and 322-427; `authored: 2` in the haptics log
findings.what: Authored feelings are shown behaving like built-ins in three paths — sitting in the Mischief grid with identical tile treatment, charging on a hold, and arriving from the far phone in two different regions with the pattern's own rhythm (measured lift onsets 16 / 320 / 608 ms against the specified 0 / 300 / 600, and peak lift scaling 11.6 px at 0.55 to 13.3 px at 0.90) — but 'every path' is not evidenced: no authored feeling appears in 12_search, in 04_moments, as a reaction, in a take-back, or in any push or pocket record, and only two exist.
findings.why: The clause says every path; three paths out of the app's many are demonstrated.

findings.where: the `felt_distance` block; the bar chart of all 36 patterns
findings.what: The separability check is sound and reproduces — I re-derived it independently and got a smallest pair of 17.47 against the file's 17.74, with the half-Weber control band topping out at 8.75 and the twice-Weber band bottoming out at 13.36, so the derived floor of 8.7 and the non-overlap both hold — but it measures pairwise discrimination, not the 36-way absolute identification the row asks for, and the strip that accompanies it plots on/off durations only, so two patterns of the same rhythm at different amplitudes are indistinguishable on it.
findings.why: 'Identifiable by its haptic pattern alone' is a naming task; what the set measures is whether two patterns can be told apart, which is a weaker claim and is the only one the numbers support.

findings.what: My eye disagrees with the held-frame number on this stretch. The three-term test passes every frame here, but only on its busiest-tile term (4.8 to 6.3 grey levels); the whole-frame mean is 0.027-0.037 and the share of pixels moving by more than two is 0.33 per cent, so 19 consecutive frames — 1.44 seconds of app time — read as a still picture to anyone watching.
findings.why: The briefing invites this: the check is a floor, not a verdict, and on this take it passes a stretch a reader sees as held.

what_is_working: A feeling genuinely arrives as a sensation and not as a coloured message. In 07_feeling_landing the whole page lifts and turns on the arriving pattern's own envelope, measured by phase correlation frame by frame: 'overwhelmed' alternates between 0 and about 11 px on every other frame for 28 frames — 14 lifts in 448 ms against a specified (18 ms on / 14 ms off) x 14; 'miss_you' lifts, decays to nothing, and lifts again with 752 ms between onsets against a specified 750; 'here' holds a lift for 416 ms, sits at zero for 400, and lifts again, against a specified 400/400; 'squeeze' makes three lifts of 6.7, 12.1 and 17.2 px against asked amplitudes of 78, 138 and 198 — ratios of 1.81 and 2.57 against 1.77 and 2.54.

It is the whole board that moves, not one card. At the peak of the 'hold' landing all six tiles of the frame shift together (dy -12.88 / -13.85 top, -12.93 / -14.05 middle, -12.47 / -13.72 bottom) while dx falls with height (-8.58, -7.14, -4.67), which is a rotation about a pivot below the screen; the implied turn is -0.0021 rad against the -0.00375 rad the haptics log claims.

The vocabulary is there and it is on the glass, not just in a log: 34 built-in feelings across six named families (Warmth 6, Ache 5, Shelter 7, Mischief 7, Static 6, Sparkle 5) in logs/haptics.json, and 15_authored_feeling opens all six family tabs in turn so every one of the 36 is visible as a named tile — including the Ache and Static families, whose eleven feelings appear nowhere else in the set.

Every feeling is a photograph or a drawing of a real thing, never an emoji or a stock illustration: logs/surfaces.json counts 36 objects named by feelings, 21 measured as real surfaces, 10 read, 5 drawn in the app with a pen. On the glass they read as a white gourd, a pink sweet, a scattering of paper confetti, a drawn chair, a rubber band, a paper crane.

Twelve partner-state signals are on the glass, not merely in a record. 01_pulse.png and crops/dusk_pulse.png both show a ruled sheet with MOOD, HERE, WHERE, NEED, ENERGY, BATTERY, LAST UP, THEIR CLOCK, RINGER, MOVING, SIGNAL and AT HOME filled in, above the status line in the couple's own words; the log carries 14 keys.

State really does propagate and is legible in three places at once. In 08_state_propagating the far phone's 'mood restless' cross-dissolves the standing-line sheet over 21 frames, and by the end of the clip the same strip reads OUT HEADS DOWN QUIET while the thread carries '— noor · out', '— noor is heads down' and '— noor is quiet' as separate rows.

The authored feeling 'tuesday soup' drives the same channel as a built-in, in two different regions, with the intensity carried: measured lift onsets of 16 / 320 / 608 ms against a specified 0 / 300 / 600, and a peak lift of 11.6 px at strength 0.55 against 13.3 px at 0.90 (asked amplitudes 98 and 123).

The link going down and coming back is on the glass in words with no product cheer: 'can't reach the other phone. it'll go when it can.', a row marked 'waiting to send', then the same row marked 'sent'. logs/strings.json applies eight anti-goal patterns across 568 read strings and returns no findings.

The build is honest about what it cannot do here. Every region report carries asked_a_motor_for with the ask and the answer written down separately, logs/reception.json says in its own words that its banner is not an iPhone banner, and 17_setup_pwa.png tells the reader on the glass that the phone 'will not hold on to anything' until the app is on the home screen.

verdict: The hardest sentence in this row is met and I can put numbers on it: a feeling sent from the far phone arrives as a photograph of a real object landing on a desk while the whole board lifts and turns on that feeling's own envelope, and the envelope is right to the frame — 'overwhelmed' gives fourteen alternating lifts in 448 ms against a specified fourteen, 'miss_you' puts 752 ms between its onsets against a specified 750, 'squeeze' steps 6.7 / 12.1 / 17.2 px against asked amplitudes of 78 / 138 / 198, and the lift is the same across the top, middle and bottom of the frame with a measured turn of -0.0021 rad, so it is the page and not a card. Thirty-four built-ins across six named families are on the glass rather than only in a log, twelve partner signals are written out on a ruled sheet, the authored 'tuesday soup' drives the same channel with the same rhythm in two different regions with its strength carried, and the state propagation clip really does change the standing line from bright to restless to quiet. What is missing is everything the row asks for once the screen is not being looked at. The pattern never reaches a finger: all fourteen motor asks in the three feeling scenes answer 'no motor in a browser', the substitute that does carry it is the page visibly moving, and with the screen face down that channel is gone by construction; the only channel that would survive — the feeling's own sound — is in the clips solely because the capture tool mixed the .ogg over silence, which its own log states, so the set contains no evidence of the app making a sound at all. That is the finding holding this row at its floor and it is marked blocking. Around it, the pocket surface reads back empty in all seventeen reports including the one built this cycle to read it back; the closed-app surface is a silent Chromium desktop toast with a blank icon and a generic line of text, which the reception log itself says is not an iPhone banner and not a lock screen; the picker corner is shown opening in two of five regions and one-gesture-ness cannot be checked because no pointer is ever drawn; and in the propagation clip the far phone's message, delivered on reconnect, lands as an empty sheet signed with the wrong name. Sixteen of twenty: an emotional nervous system that is real and measurable while you are watching it, and undemonstrated the moment you are not.
